newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen gets $26.5 million Japanese grant for reform.
newsitem.headline: Yemen gets $26.5 million Japanese grant for reform.

text.p: Japan agreed on Thursday to grant Yemen $26.5 million to assist its IMF-agreed economic reforms and allow it buy modern agricultural machinery to boost wheat and corn production.
The deal was signed by Abdul-Qader Bagammal, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Planning and Development and Japan's ambassador to Yemen, the official news agency SABA added.
The $22 million grant, Japan's first to Yemen, will help boost Yemen's economic restructuring programme supervised by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
The rest will be spent on purchasing farm machinery and pesticides to help the impoverished Arab state increase its agricultural output, especially wheat and corn, SABA said.
Japan has since the 1980s given Yemen $4.5 million every year to help it increase its agricultural production.
